sources.pylons: w-f16, mf-f16i, aft-f16i, ipms-f16i, inferred, f16net-aim9, f16net-aim120

notes.type: the F-16's type code, the one the shared code keys the F-16 family on; the airframe definition f16i makes it the Sufa
notes.model: none: the player's jet is drawn from its airframe definition (shared/extra/planes/f16i/airframe.json)
notes.scale: 1: our models are built true size
notes.radius_m: half the span over the wingtip rails, 9.96 m
notes.strength: our damage scale's fighter (iaf-2026/docs/data-formats.md, damage scale)
notes.loadout.20mm: M61A1, 511 rounds (the F-16's; the two-seat Sufa's count is not published, inferred the same)
notes.loadout.chaff: no public count found; 60 held until one is
notes.loadout.flare: no public count found; 60 held until one is
notes.pylons: an AIM-9M on each wingtip rail (stations 1 and 9, A and I): the F-16's wingtip rails carry its short-range missiles; the Sufa's two wingtip missiles are standard (mf-f16i), its usual one the Python 5 (aft-f16i), which the sim has no record of yet, so the AIM-9M stands in (inferred); a 370 US gal tank on each wing's inboard station (stations 4 and 6, D and F; the Sufa's options list two 370 gal wing tanks, ipms-f16i), carried on most flights (inferred); no other underwing stores in training (inferred); an AIM-9M on each underwing missile station, 2 / 8 (B, H) and 3 / 7 (C, G): the F-16 carries AIM-9s and AIM-120s there (f16net-aim9, f16net-aim120); on 2 / 8 the AIM-9M stands in for the IAF's Python (aft-f16i on the Sufa, inferred on the Barak), on 3 / 7 for an AIM-120, which the sim has no record of yet (stand-ins, inferred)

footnotes.w-f16: Wikipedia, "General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon" (span 32 ft 8 in, 9.96 m), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Dynamics_F-16_Fighting_Falcon
footnotes.gdots-f16: General Dynamics OTS, "F-16 20mm Gatling gun system" (511 rounds), https://www.gd-ots.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/11/F-16.pdf
footnotes.mf-f16i: MilitaryFactory, "Lockheed F-16I Sufa (Storm)" (2 x short-range air-to-air missiles on wingtip launchers), https://www.militaryfactory.com/aircraft/detail.php?aircraft_id=2191
footnotes.ipms-f16i: IPMS USA, "F-16I Sufa Part 1" (the Sufa's stores: 2 x 370 gallon wing tanks, 2 x 600 gallon wing tanks), https://reviews.ipmsusa.org/review/f-16i-sufa-part-1
footnotes.aft-f16i: Airforce Technology, "F-16I Soufa Multirole Fighter, Israel" (equipped with the Rafael Python 5), https://www.airforce-technology.com/projects/f-16i-soufa/
footnotes.f16net-aim9: F-16.net, "AIM-9 Sidewinder" (stations 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7; one missile each), https://www.f-16.net/f-16_armament_article1.html
footnotes.f16net-aim120: F-16.net, "AIM-120 AMRAAM" (stations 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7; one missile each), https://www.f-16.net/f-16_armament_article3.html
